title: Classes as Blueprints
summary: Understand what a class really is: a reusable blueprint or template. Learn how to write your own class with properties and behaviors.
learningObjectives: Understand the core definition: a class is a blueprint or template
Identify properties (fields) and behaviors (methods) inside a class
Write a clean Java class declaration from scratch without fear
expectedOutcomes: Clear understanding that writing a class does not create an object yet
Ability to write a valid class blueprint with fields and methods in Java

activities.title: The Architect's Blueprint vs The Real House

analogy.headline: You cannot sleep inside an architect's paper drawing
analogy.story:
Before an architect builds a house, they draw a blueprint on paper.

The blueprint describes everything the house will have: 3 bedrooms, 2 bathrooms, a front door, and a garage. It also describes what the house can do: turn on lights, open doors, ring doorbell.

Can you sleep inside that paper blueprint? Can you park your car in it? Of course not! It is just a plan — a description.

To live in a house, a construction crew must use the blueprint to construct the actual physical building of bricks and wood.

In Java:
- **Class** = The Blueprint on paper.
- **Object** = The Real House built from that blueprint!
analogy.keyTakeaway: A class is a design template that describes what properties and behaviors an object will have. The class itself is not the actual object.

activities.title: Anatomy of a Java Class

keyTakeaways: A class is a blueprint describing what properties (fields) and actions (methods) an entity has
Declaring a class allocates zero object memory in RAM
Methods inside a class have direct access to its fields without passing parameters
Java class names always use PascalCase (e.g. StudentRecord, BankAccount)

activities.title: A Complete Blueprint Example: The Book Class
activities.description: Observe how natural the Book blueprint is. Any book in the world has a title, an author, and a number of pages. The class simply groups these related attributes into a clean, reusable blueprint.

activities.title: Concept Validation: Classes as Blueprints (10 Questions)

questions.prompt: What is the primary role of a class in Java?
options: It acts as a blueprint or template that defines properties and behaviors for objects
It compiles computer hardware drivers directly
It stores numbers in RAM immediately upon declaration
questions.explanation: A class is a design blueprint from which objects are created.

hints.hint: Think of the architectural floor plan.

questions.prompt: When you write 'class Car { String brand; int speed; }', does a real car exist in RAM yet?
options: No, you have only written the template describing what a Car has
Yes, but only if the file name is Car.java
No, classes can never create objects
questions.explanation: Defining a class does not allocate object instances in memory. It only describes the template.

hints.hint: A paper blueprint is not a physical house.

questions.prompt: What do variables declared directly inside a class represent?
options: Properties / Fields / State of the object
questions.explanation: Variables declared inside a class define the properties (state) that every object of that class will hold.

questions.prompt: What do methods declared inside a class represent?
options: Behaviors / Actions the object can perform
questions.explanation: Methods inside a class define the actions (behaviors) the object can execute.

questions.prompt: What naming convention is standard for Java class names?
questions.explanation: Java classes are named using PascalCase (each word starts with a capital letter, like Student, BankAccount).

questions.prompt: Can methods inside a class directly use fields of the same class without receiving them as arguments?
options: Yes, because the method and fields live inside the same class scope
No, Java requires every variable to be passed as a method argument
Only if the method returns an integer
questions.explanation: Instance methods have direct access to instance fields of the class without needing extra parameters.

hints.hint: Methods and fields belong to the same blueprint.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a valid class declaration in Java?
questions.explanation: In Java, classes are declared using the 'class' keyword followed by the identifier and curly braces.

questions.prompt: Can a class contain multiple methods?
options: No, Java only allows exactly 1 method per class
Yes, a class can have as many methods as needed to model its behaviors
Only if all methods return void
questions.explanation: A class can contain as many fields and methods as needed to represent the entity accurately.

questions.prompt: If you write a class without constructors or access modifiers, will it still compile and work?
options: No, Java requires private and constructors for every class
Yes, Java provides clean default settings so beginner classes compile and run smoothly
Only if you install external packages
questions.explanation: Java is designed so simple classes with fields and methods compile and run without needing advanced boilerplate.

questions.prompt: What is the relationship between a class and a custom data type?
options: A class defines a brand new reference data type in Java (e.g., Student is a type just like String)
Classes can only represent primitive integers
questions.explanation: When you define 'class Student', you are introducing 'Student' as a new custom data type in your program!

hints.hint: Student is now a valid type.

interviewQA.question: What is a class in Java?
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: A class is a user-defined blueprint or template from which individual objects are created. It specifies the properties (variables) and behaviors (methods) that all objects of that type will possess.
keyPoints: Does not allocate object data in memory until an object is instantiated

interviewQA.question: Does writing a class allocate memory for objects?
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: No. Defining a class simply introduces the type and structure to the Java compiler. Memory for actual object data is only allocated when you explicitly create an instance using the 'new' keyword.
keyPoints: Zero object memory on class definition
Memory is allocated dynamically at runtime with 'new'

interviewQA.question: What is the difference between a class and a structure in languages like C?
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: In C, a struct only holds data variables and cannot contain methods directly. In Java, a class holds both data (state) and methods (behavior) together, enabling true object-oriented encapsulation.
keyPoints: C structs traditionally hold only data
Java classes combine data and behavior into a cohesive entity

interviewQA.question: Why should class names follow PascalCase in Java?
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: PascalCase (e.g. StudentProfile, BankAccount) is the universal Java standard. It immediately helps developers and tools distinguish class types from variable names and method names, which use camelCase.
keyPoints: Distinguishes types from variables and methods

interviewQA.question: Can a Java class have fields without methods or methods without fields?
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: Yes! A class with only fields is often used as a simple data holder. A class with only methods can act as a utility or service provider. However, classic OOP classes typically bundle both fields and methods together.
keyPoints: Classes can have fields only, methods only, or both
Full OOP pairs state with behaviors that operate on that state

interviewQA.question: How many classes can you write in a single Java program?
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: As many as your application requires! Large enterprise applications routinely have thousands of classes, each modeling a distinct entity or component of the system.
keyPoints: No practical limit to the number of classes
Each class should represent a clear single concept

activities.title: Lesson 3 Checkpoint
checklist: I can explain the difference between a blueprint and an actual object.
I can write a class in Java with properties and a simple method.
I understand that defining a class does not automatically create an object in memory.

practiceProblems.title: Fix Broken Class Syntax
practiceProblems.description: A junior developer wrote: 'Class dog ( string name, int age ) { void bark() [ System.out.println("Woof"); ] }'. Fix the syntax errors by using lowercase 'class', uppercase 'String', curly braces '{ }', and normal class structure. In Main, print 'Dog class fixed!'.
practiceProblems.problemStatement: A junior developer wrote: 'Class dog ( string name, int age ) { void bark() [ System.out.println("Woof"); ] }'. Fix the syntax errors by using lowercase 'class', uppercase 'String', curly braces '{ }', and normal class structure. In Main, print 'Dog class fixed!'.
practiceProblems.hint: Use 'class Dog { String name; int age; void bark() { System.out.println("Woof"); } }'.
hints: Use 'class Dog { String name; int age; void bark() { System.out.println("Woof"); } }'.
